script.base: Morning-of read only: PIT -3.5, total 39, implied PIT 21.2 / CLE 17.8, outdoor conditions with wind 5.4 mph and 67.4F so weather is not the script. Most likely flow is a modest PIT lead in a low-event game. PIT leans run with Jaylen Warren (47 carries, 252 rush yards in weeks 5-7, about 15.7 carries and 5.4 YPC) against a CLE run defense that has allowed 4.58 YPC and 28 runs of 10+. Aaron Rodgers does not need a shootout; Germie Bernard (26 targets, 194 yards) and DK Metcalf (L3 games that sum to his 161 yards are 12, 93, 56) are secondary to the grind. CLE, a 3.5 dog that cannot feature Quinshon Judkins into PIT's 3.87 YPC run defense, mixes Deshaun Watson scrambles (L3 rush games summing to 88 are 40, 29, 19) with a crowded pass game, but a 17.8 team total caps it.
script.flip1: CLE hangs around or leads, PIT cannot clock-kill, and Rodgers is pushed into a CLE blitz look he has been bad against (PIT EPA/dropback -0.30 vs blitz, -0.02 vs no blitz; CLE blitz rate 24%). Warren's rush line dies toward the 50-yard game already inside weeks 5-7, and Bernard, Metcalf, Pat Freiermuth and Jaylen Warren checkdowns absorb the extra dropbacks.
script.flip2: PIT jumps ahead early, Warren's late snaps get cut for Rico Dowdle (16 carries / 81 rush yards in the same three-week window), and CLE garbage-time throws finally convert Denzel Boston's empty air (315 air yards, only 88 receiving yards in weeks 5-7). Starter unders and the lead-back over can both lose late even if the first half looked like a slog.

PIT's chart is Warren over Dowdle, with Rodgers, Metcalf, Bernard, Freiermuth and Darnell Washington all on the target/carry sheet. No next-man-up edge.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Location YPA only. PIT defense: left 6.88 on 110 attempts, middle 7.58 on 45, right 6.10 on 84. CLE defense: left 6.41 on 88, middle 8.30 on 47, right 5.85 on 101. Both bleed the middle on a small sample; the outside right is the tighter side for each.
matchup.pressure: PIT blitzes 27%. CLE EPA/dropback is -0.09 vs blitz and +0.07 with no blitz, so pressure is a mild negative for Watson and should shorten throws toward Harold Fannin, Judkins and McLaughlin rather than Boston's deep air. CLE blitzes only 24%. PIT EPA/dropback is -0.30 vs blitz and -0.02 with no blitz, so a blitz would push Rodgers to checkdowns (Warren -26 air yards, Bernard), but 24% is not a pressure-heavy plan.
matchup.bleeds: CLE's real bleed is the run: 4.58 YPC and 28 runs of 10+ over 7 games, plus middle passing at 8.30 YPA. PIT's bleed is the middle at 7.58 YPA on only 45 throws; their run defense is the strength at 3.87 YPC and 17 runs of 10+. Explosives: PIT has allowed 23 passes of 20+ for 257 yards, CLE 20 for 256.
matchup.overlap: The only confirmed overlap is PIT's lead runner, Jaylen Warren, into CLE's weak run front. Bernard is PIT's target leader (26 targets) and CLE's middle is soft, but with no shell chart that is a hypothesis, not a leg. CLE's target leader Boston (20 targets, 315 air, 88 yards) is not efficiently attacking PIT's middle leak.

form: Avoiding season averages. Warren rush last4 is 93, 101, 50, 101; the three that sum to the weeks 5-7 total of 252 are 101, 50, 101 (median 101, one miss at 50). He still owns the backfield, 47 carries to Dowdle's 16. Warren receiving last4 33, 87, 28, 36, all over 22.5; weeks 5-7 subset is 87, 28, 36. Dowdle rush+rec last4 21, 44, 49, 86 sits mostly under 49.5 but the 86 and rush games of 40 and 41 block a second leg. Metcalf's weeks 5-7 trio is 12, 93, 56 against a 53.5 line (the 115 is outside that window) — a fair number. Bernard's weeks 5-7 trio is 80, 87, 27 against 44, hot but unpriced and one dud. Boston's weeks 5-7 trio is 46, 15, 27, all under 47.5, but 315 air yards plus PIT's 23 explosives make the under a one-play fade. Concepcion's weeks 5-7 trio is 5, 37, 129 and Jeudy's is 19, 69, 21 — averages inflated by one spike, not overs. Fannin's weeks 5-7 trio is 4, 9, 91, same spike problem. Judkins last4 rush 70, 53, 44, 96 does not reconcile to the listed 31/140, so he is not used. Sampson is a one-game sample. No similar-defense game logs beyond these splits.

pro_edge.script_read: Low total means fewer plays, run-heavy lean, not a volume-over shootout. Spread is 3.5, so the dog-throws-more rule applies to CLE targets, but the 17.8 cap stops that from being an automatic WR over stack. Leader-runs-late points at Warren's carries. Blowout flag is mild at 3.5; late snap risk is the flip, not the base. Build usage from shares: Warren 47 of about 63 RB carries in the three-week window, not from a season average.
pro_edge.best_price: No saved price beats a sharp anchor by a real margin. Pinnacle is not in the pack; anchor is consensus no-vig, and every two-sided prop is 0.492-0.508. Best tags are -110 to -116.5. Selected leg: Jaylen Warren rush yards over 64.5 at -115.5 versus consensus no-vig over 0.504 (the under is the cheaper side at -111.5, which is the other way). No two-sided price on Rico Dowdle receiving yards 15, Quinshon Judkins rush yards 47, or Germie Bernard receiving yards 44. No alt +300 'value' in the inputs. Power devig versus overround not separately provided.
pro_edge.lagging: No lagging-line flags in the precomputed scan. No open-to-current spread or total move, and no prop-that-failed-to-move table. Cannot call a book off consensus.
pro_edge.sleepers: None. Official injury report: none listed. No OUT/Doubtful/IR player and no same-position teammate whose line failed to move. Sampson's thin log is a sample-size issue, not a sleeper from a ruled-out starter.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Warren clears 64.5 rush yards because a 21.2-point PIT favorite in a 39-total game should hand him the clock, and he is running into the soft spot on this sheet — CLE has allowed 4.58 yards per carry and 28 runs of 10+ — after rush games of 93, 101, 50 and 101 with 47 carries in the last three team games.
edge_players.must_be_true: Warren is active with no snap cap (injury report blank), keeps something like the recent 47-to-16 carry split over Dowdle, and PIT is not trailing long enough to abandon the run. About 13 carries at his recent 5.4 YPC clears 64.5; CLE's 4.58 YPC allowed says efficiency should not fall apart.
edge_players.kills_it: Flip 1: CLE stays close or leads, Rodgers throws, and Warren repeats the in-window 50-yard game. Also killed if Dowdle's 40- and 41-yard rush games steal a third of the work, or a real blowout sits Warren before the volume stacks. Tagged script-dependent on PIT not trailing; it still survives the base script and the blowout flip if the carries come early.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Warren under 64.5 lost. CLE sold out to the run after an early gash, or flip 1 hit: Cleveland stayed within a score, Rodgers threw 35-plus times, and Warren finished on about 11 carries for 50 — the miss already inside weeks 5-7. Dowdle posted another 40-yard rush day and a few checkdowns, so the bellcow read was a committee. The market had the over at 0.504 no-vig and was right to shrug. No front-seven charting was available to test whether CLE's 4.58 YPC was a stale seven-game number rather than the current front. That counter is real, which is why this is flagged, but it is not stronger than the base read of lead-back volume into a bad run defense in a 21-point team total.
slip_story: One story only: PIT modest lead, run the clock, low total 39. Warren rush over is the favorite-runs anchor. Do not pair it with CLE receiver overs, a game total over, or a second Warren market. Complementary unders (Freiermuth, Washington, Dowdle) fit the story on paper and were left off because their pre-mortems were as strong as the reads. No TD legs. Single-leg slip until a second name clears step 10.
